beats: Hook: send each bit three times and take a vote: at a 1% error rate failures drop to about 0.03%; at 60% the vote makes things worse. Where is the crossover, and does the trick survive the jump to qubits? (line_qc_vote_switch_fix, then the cover; reuse line_qc_analog_pigeon_vote, the QC01-03 callback: "send 000, vote at the other end".) Cast for QC08-01 to QC08-04 (lecture Q25-10, and the start of Q25-11 that finishes its story), described in full in every prompt: the keeper = the code (encodes, checks, fixes; chin-length hair with one hair clip, a zip-up work overall, a torch on the chest pocket, work boots) and the imp = the noise (knee-high, bean-shaped, big pointed ears, curly tail; the narration may call it a gremlin, the prompts never do). Bits are toggle switches on wall plates, the props of QC06-02's parity hallway; in this classical part the plates have no covers, so the keeper can simply look. Invented characters only: no lecturer figure, never her likeness; her voice and slides carry her part.

Why a course of its own (00:07-01:10) and why it is needed (02:00-02:29): her illustration, hardware at about 1e-5 errors per operation against a need of 1e-15 or better; a program is an endless row of switches and one slip spoils it (line_qc_vote_long_hall; reuse line_qc_surf_stepping_stones, QC03-04: every stone has to hold).

Repetition and majority vote (02:57-04:28; tape Q24-09 p2): store each bit on three switches; when one disagrees, set it back to match the other two (line_qc_vote_switch_fix; the code letters 0 0 0 -> 0 1 0 -> 0 0 0 over the levers).

Physical vs logical error (04:28-06:43): the imp flips each switch on its own, with probability p each (line_qc_vote_imp_dice: one die per switch); the vote is right when none or one flipped: P(correct) = (1-p)^3 + 3p(1-p)^2, so it fails with 3p^2 - 2p^3 (p = 0.01: 0.000298). Two flips fool it, and the keeper "fixes" the one good switch (line_qc_vote_two_flipped).

A threshold (06:43-07:59; Q24-09 28:06-29:56; clips Q25-10 07:34-07:59 and Q24-09 28:06-28:32): voting helps only while p < 1/2; at p = 0.6 it fails 64.8% of the time, worse than one switch (line_qc_vote_calm_vs_swarm; the code plots 3p^2 - 2p^3 against p, crossing the diagonal at 1/2; reuse line_balance for the tipping point). The simplest error threshold; real codes' thresholds are far lower and depend on the noise model (QC01-03).

Bit flips happen to qubits too, but a qubit cannot be copied (07:59-14:07; Q24-09 06:57-11:04; reuse line_qc_cnot_copier_envelope, QC05-04). Fan-out instead: two CNOTs turn alpha|0> + beta|1> (plus two |0> helpers) into alpha|000> + beta|111>, repeating only the basis states (clip Q25-10 12:48-13:13: "the Bell circuit plus one more CNOT"; line_qc_vote_triple_machine: QC06-02's pairing machine with a third funnel; reuse line_qc_pair_machine; tape Q24-09 p4, p5). Honest caveat in the narration: the three lidded cups match only when read the 0/1 way; it is one shared state, not three copies of the qubit. Avoid Q24-09 00:05-00:33 (quiz logistics).
Cover (line_qc_cover_08_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the imp has flipped the middle one of three switches; the keeper, unbothered, points at the two that still agree.
